name: dsh-vsc
description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) in VS Code: native sidebar panel + editor bridge for the local AI agent — a pure protocol client, no second server.
author: zhibailu

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Pure bridge to the local DSH harness (127.0.0.1:3080): panel, status bar, editor context. No workspace code is executed.

dshVsc.url.description: Base URL of the DSH harness this extension talks to. Default 3080 = the web GUI's harness: the extension connects as a shared client and never starts or kills it. If nothing answers there, the extension auto-starts its own instance (recorded in %TEMP%\dsh-vsc-harness.pid, stopped when VS Code exits). Also honors DSH_WEB_URL.

dshVsc.autoStart.description: Start `dsh web` automatically when no harness is reachable at the configured URL.

dshVsc.token.description: Since DSH 0.2.1, every /api call and event stream requires a cookie exchanged for the token printed by `dsh web` at launch. A harness this extension starts itself reads the token from its launch output, so nothing needs filling in; only when you started `dsh web` manually (or connect to an instance inside WSL) do you paste that token=… URL or the token itself here. The token changes on every launch.

dshVsc.language.description: Language of this extension's own UI: panel, settings tab, status bar, and the notifications and errors the host raises. `zh` renders upstream's strings untouched. The harness's own output (agent replies, tool output) is not translated. Changing it rebuilds the panel, which reloads its state.

dshVsc.maxAttachMB.description: Upper size limit in MB for anything this extension reads for you: images referenced by path, images pasted from the clipboard, and files dropped onto the panel. 0 disables the limit (you know what you are doing). This is a transport guard — the harness enforces its own admission limits on images, and stores generic files verbatim regardless.

enumDescriptions: Up/Down walk the prompt history, like a terminal (default)
Up/Down move the caret inside the prompt, like a text editor
dshVsc.promptArrowKeys.description: What the Up/Down arrows do in the composer. history keeps the terminal behaviour this panel shipped with; caret gives the arrows back to the text, so the caret can move through a multi-line draft.

dshVsc.messageTimestamps.description: Show wall-clock times in the transcript: every user message, and each turn (“Round N · HH:MM”) for the agent side. Times come from the session log’s own event timestamps, so history replays identically.

scripts.package: npm run gen:i18n && node esbuild.js && vsce package --no-dependencies
